reasons: 3a. Do both dimensions share HB-E1? — CONDITION_MET.
Yes. The qualifier-loss comparison uses HB-E1 against AJR-E2 in both dimensions. Assigning that shared comparison to “Claim mutation” is reasonable and avoids counting the same mismatch twice.
3b. Is there distinct inferential work, and has the nesting accounted for it? — CONDITION_NOT_MET.
The hub row contains an additional proposition: the synthesis reaches citing works that do not cite the designated primary-paper record.
That proposition uses separate evidence:
recent_all_HB.json: 1,676 recent works citing either hub version.
recent_cocite_HB.json: 276 of those also citing AJR record W3124166904.
Difference: 1,400.
Claim mutation establishes a change in wording. These counts describe a citation-distribution pattern. Neither proposition alone establishes the other.

The 1,400 figure is a database-specific citation count. It does not establish that those works repeated the disputed claim, relied on that passage, or failed to inspect AJR. The audit acknowledges part of this limitation at line 206.

The nesting rationale nevertheless says only that both dimensions share HB-E1. It does not evaluate the additional reach evidence or explain why that evidence supplies no independently countable inference. The reach claim remains visible in the report, so it was not deleted; its possible contribution to the aggregate was excluded without an adequate substantive explanation.

This finding does not automatically justify counting the whole hub dimension separately. The appropriate repair is to distinguish the shared wording mismatch from the reach claim, then assess whether the latter supports independent concern.
